$schema-note: Teyla brand tokens, proposal. One set for the Mac app, the CLI, the plugin and the web. Contrast ratios are WCAG 2.x, measured against background (bg) and surface (sf).

mark.note: Logo-only colours. Graphics need 3:1, not 4.5:1, so the light-mode accent in the mark is brighter than the needs-you text colour.

ansi256.note: xterm-256 indices for the CLI. Pick the set from the terminal background (COLORFGBG, or a --theme flag); when unknown, use the ansi16 fallback. Contrast is against #FFFFFF (light) and #1E1E1E (dark).
ansi256.glyph: The one-character mark for banners depends on the chosen concept: 1 = three ━ rows and ●, 2 = ◔, 3 = bold T followed by █ in needs-you.

type.sans: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "SF Pro Text", Inter, system-ui, "Segoe UI", sans-serif
type.mono: ui-monospace, "SF Mono", Menlo, "JetBrains Mono", Consolas, monospace
type.note: System fonts only: nothing to bundle or license. SF Pro on Apple platforms, Inter where a web page wants one font everywhere. The wordmark is drawn as paths and needs no font.

recommendation: Concept 3, Cursor, is the strongest mark: at 16 px it is still a solid T and one block, and a T followed by a cursor block is a one-character terminal banner that no other concept can match. Its amber block says "waiting on you" in the language developers already read, a cursor waiting for input, without a speech bubble. Lanes turns into a hamburger-menu icon at small sizes, and Meter reads as a generic speedometer, so both need more explaining than Cursor does.
